claim: AAV-sgNGL2-tdT removed NGL2 from horizontal cells with 95% efficiency when injected at P0 in Cas9 mice.
source: The NGL2 intensity at axon tips of tdT-positive horizontal cells in Cas9 mice was lower than at neighboring axon tips in 19 of 20 cells (i.e., 95% of cells, Figure 1B and C)
evidence: Experimental data showing NGL2 intensity reduction in 19 of 20 infected cells, with statistical significance (p<0.01 for each cell)

claim: Multiple horizontal cells co-innervate more than 40% of rods in their shared territory.
source: Co-injection of AAVs expressing spectrally separable fluorophores (cyan fluorescent protein [CFP] and tdT) revealed that overlapping horizontal cell axons co-innervate more than 40% of the rods in their shared territory (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: Direct experimental observation using dual-color AAV labeling to visualize overlapping horizontal cell axons

claim: Horizontal cell axons cover the retina approximately ninefold as a population.
source: As a population, horizontal cell axons cover the retina approximately ninefold (Soto et al., 2013; Keeley et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: NGL2 regulates horizontal cell axon development cell-autonomously.
source: Thus, during development, NGL2 appears to selectively and cell-autonomously regulate the growth of horizontal cell axons and the formation of synapses between horizontal cell axons and rods.
evidence: Based on experimental data showing that removal of NGL2 from individual horizontal cells produces the same phenotypes as germline knockout

claim: Developmental removal of NGL2 from individual horizontal cells increases axon territory size in Cas9 mice but not in wild-type mice.
source: In wild-type mice, P0 injection of AAV-sgNGL2-tdT affected neither the size of horizontal cell axons nor the density of their tips at P30 (Figure 2A, B, F and G). In Cas9 mice, axons of horizontal cells infected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT were larger and had fewer tips than axons of horizontal cells infected with AAV-YFP (Figure 2C–2G).
evidence: Quantitative measurements of axon territories and tip densities with statistical comparisons between groups

claim: Developmental removal of NGL2 from individual horizontal cells reduces axon tip density in Cas9 mice but not in wild-type mice.
source: In wild-type mice, P0 injection of AAV-sgNGL2-tdT affected neither the size of horizontal cell axons nor the density of their tips at P30 (Figure 2A, B, F and G). In Cas9 mice, axons of horizontal cells infected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT were larger and had fewer tips than axons of horizontal cells infected with AAV-YFP (Figure 2C–2G).
evidence: Quantitative measurements showing reduced tip density in Cas9 mice with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT compared to AAV-YFP controls

claim: Changes in horizontal cell axon size and tip density in Cas9 mice injected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT match those observed in germline Ngl2 knockout mice.
source: Changes in horizontal cell axon size and tip density in Cas9 mice injected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT matched those observed in germline Ngl2 knockout mice (Ngl2-/- mice) (Soto et al., 2013).
evidence: Comparison to previously published data from germline knockout mice

claim: Nearly all horizontal cell axon tips appose ribbon release sites of rod photoreceptors in both wild-type and Cas9 mice injected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT.
source: Both in wild-type mice and in Cas9 mice injected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT, nearly all horizontal cell axon tips apposed ribbon release sites of rod photoreceptors (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Immunostaining data showing colocalization of axon tips with Bassoon-labeled presynaptic ribbons (96.7% and 97.7% respectively)

claim: Removal of NGL2 from individual horizontal cells does not affect the size of horizontal cell dendrites or the number of their contacts with cones.
source: Consistent with our findings in Ngl2-/- mice (Soto et al., 2013), removal of NGL2 from individual horizontal cells did not affect the size of horizontal cell dendrites or the number of their contacts with cones (Figure 2H–2N).
evidence: Quantitative measurements showing no significant differences in dendrite territories or terminal clusters across genotypes and AAVs (p>0.9 for all comparisons)

claim: NGL2 maintains horizontal cell axon tips and restrains axon growth in mature circuits.
source: To test whether NGL2 contributes to the maintenance of horizontal cell axons and synapses, we injected AAV-sgNGL2-tdT in P30 (i.e., young adult) Cas9 mice. By P60, axon arbors of tdT-positive horizontal cells had expanded and lost many tips, compared to Cas9 mice injected with AAV-YFP (Figure 3A–3E).
evidence: Experimental data showing axon expansion and tip loss after NGL2 removal in mature circuits

claim: Phenotypes produced by NGL2 removal in mature circuits are stable over time.
source: Axon expansion and tip loss were stable at P90 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating that the same phenotypes produced by developmental NGL2 removal emerge rapidly and persist after removal of NGL2 in mature circuits.
evidence: Longitudinal data showing persistence of phenotypes from P60 to P90

claim: NGL2 signaling restrains horizontal cell axon growth and maintains synapses between horizontal cells and rods throughout adulthood.
source: Strikingly, by P180, horizontal cell axons had expanded and lost tips to the same degree observed for developmental and young adult manipulations (Figure 4A–4E). Injection of AAV-sgNGL2-tdT in P150 wild-type mice produced no phenotypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). Thus, NGL2 signaling appears to restrain horizontal cell axon growth and to maintain synapses between horizontal cells and rods throughout adulthood.
evidence: Experimental data from P150 injections showing phenotypes at P180, with appropriate controls

claim: Neuronal morphology and connectivity in the outer retina are mature 3-4 weeks after birth in mice.
source: In mice, neuronal morphology and connectivity in the outer retina are mature 3–4 weeks after birth (Huckfeldt et al., 2009; Poché et al., 2007; Blanks et al., 1974).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple previous studies

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 in Ngl2-/- mice restores horizontal cell axon size to wild-type levels.
source: In Ngl2-/- mice, AAV-NGL2 restored the size of horizontal cell axons to wild-type levels and increased the density of axon tips beyond wild-type levels (Figure 5A–5D, F and G).
evidence: Quantitative measurements showing restoration of axon territories to wild-type levels (p=1 for comparison to WT YFP)

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 in Ngl2-/- mice increases axon tip density beyond wild-type levels.
source: In Ngl2-/- mice, AAV-NGL2 restored the size of horizontal cell axons to wild-type levels and increased the density of axon tips beyond wild-type levels (Figure 5A–5D, F and G).
evidence: Quantitative measurements showing tip density in Ngl2-/- NGL2 exceeds WT YFP (p<10−6)

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 in wild-type mice elevates axon tip density without significantly changing axon size.
source: In wild-type mice, AAV-NGL2 did not significantly change horizontal cell axon size but elevated axon tip density (Figure 5D–5G).
evidence: Quantitative measurements showing no significant change in axon size (p=0.48) but increased tip density (p<0.001)

claim: A threshold amount of NGL2 is required to restrict horizontal cell axon growth.
source: The most parsimonious explanation for these findings is that a threshold amount of NGL2 is required to restrict horizontal cell axon growth and that NGL2 protein levels control synapse density bidirectionally.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that overexpression increases synapse density but doesn't further reduce axon size in wild-type mice

claim: NGL2 protein levels control synapse density bidirectionally.
source: The most parsimonious explanation for these findings is that a threshold amount of NGL2 is required to restrict horizontal cell axon growth and that NGL2 protein levels control synapse density bidirectionally.
evidence: Inference based on data showing that both re-expression in knockouts and overexpression in wild-type increase synapse density

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 exceeded wild-type protein levels at P30 after P0 injection.
source: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 exceeded wild-type protein levels at P30 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Immunostaining images showing saturated NGL2 signals in AAV-infected cells compared to wild-type levels

claim: Re-expression of NGL2 in mature horizontal cells in adult Ngl2-/- circuits can reverse axonal and synaptic phenotypes.
source: We next explored whether restoring NGL2 to individual horizontal cells in adult Ngl2-/- circuits could reverse axonal and synaptic phenotypes. Indeed, injection of AAV-NGL2 at P30 reduced axon size and increased the density of axon tips of infected horizontal cells in Ngl2-/- mice to wild-type levels by P60 (Figure 6A–D, F and G).
evidence: Experimental data showing restoration of both axon size and tip density to wild-type levels after P30 injection

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 after P30 injections exceeded wild-type protein levels by P60.
source: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 after P30 injections exceeded wild-type protein levels by P60 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Immunostaining images showing saturated NGL2 signals in AAV-infected cells compared to wild-type levels

claim: Re- and overexpression of NGL2 in mature horizontal cells can shrink axons back to their normal size in Ngl2-/- mice.
source: Thus, re- and overexpression of NGL2 in mature horizontal cells shrink axons back to their normal size in Ngl2-/- mice, and can restore and even enhance their connectivity in Ngl2-/- and wild-type mice.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings showing axon shrinkage and connectivity restoration

claim: Re- and overexpression of NGL2 in mature horizontal cells can restore and enhance connectivity in Ngl2-/- and wild-type mice.
source: Thus, re- and overexpression of NGL2 in mature horizontal cells shrink axons back to their normal size in Ngl2-/- mice, and can restore and even enhance their connectivity in Ngl2-/- and wild-type mice.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings showing connectivity restoration and enhancement

claim: NGL2 is a synaptic CAM with an extracellular leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain.
source: Netrin-G ligand 2 (NGL2), a synaptic CAM with an extracellular leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain, regulates synapse development in the hippocampus and the retina (DeNardo et al., 2012; Nishimura-Akiyoshi et al., 2007; Soto et al., 2013).
evidence: Established knowledge about NGL2 structure supported by citations

claim: NGL2 regulates synapse development in the hippocampus and the retina.
source: Netrin-G ligand 2 (NGL2), a synaptic CAM with an extracellular leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain, regulates synapse development in the hippocampus and the retina (DeNardo et al., 2012; Nishimura-Akiyoshi et al., 2007; Soto et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: In the hippocampus, NGL2 localizes to the proximal segments of CA1 pyramidal neuron dendrites.
source: In the hippocampus, NGL2 localizes to the proximal segments of CA1 pyramidal neuron dendrites and promotes the formation of synapses with Schaffer collateral axons (DeNardo et al., 2012; Nishimura-Akiyoshi et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: In the hippocampus, NGL2 promotes the formation of synapses with Schaffer collateral axons.
source: In the hippocampus, NGL2 localizes to the proximal segments of CA1 pyramidal neuron dendrites and promotes the formation of synapses with Schaffer collateral axons (DeNardo et al., 2012; Nishimura-Akiyoshi et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: In the retina, NGL2 localizes to the axon tips of horizontal cells.
source: In the retina, NGL2 localizes to the axon tips of horizontal cells and promotes the formation of synapses with rod photoreceptors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Soto et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation and immunostaining images showing NGL2 localization

claim: In the retina, NGL2 promotes the formation of synapses between horizontal cells and rod photoreceptors.
source: In the retina, NGL2 localizes to the axon tips of horizontal cells and promotes the formation of synapses with rod photoreceptors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Soto et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation and experimental data from this study

claim: Synaptic CAMs promote synapse formation in the developing nervous system.
source: Synaptic cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) promote synapse formation in the developing nervous system.
evidence: General statement about synaptic CAMs based on established scientific knowledge

claim: Most in vivo studies of synaptic CAMs have compared connectivity of wild-type and germline knockout mice.
source: Most in vivo studies of synaptic CAMs have compared connectivity of wild-type and germline knockout mice, which remove synaptic CAMs from all cells throughout life.
evidence: Statement about the state of the field based on review of literature

claim: Synapse loss can long precede cell death in neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Synapse loss can long precede cell death in neurodegenerative diseases, and the ability to establish connections with mature circuits limits benefits from transplantation of stem-cell-derived neuronal replacements (Buckingham et al., 2008; Gamm et al., 2015; Hong et al., 2016; Scheff et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: The ability to establish connections with mature circuits limits benefits from transplantation of stem-cell-derived neuronal replacements.
source: Synapse loss can long precede cell death in neurodegenerative diseases, and the ability to establish connections with mature circuits limits benefits from transplantation of stem-cell-derived neuronal replacements (Buckingham et al., 2008; Gamm et al., 2015; Hong et al., 2016; Scheff et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: Stray processes were less abundant in horizontal cells targeted by AAV-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 strategy compared to germline Ngl2-/- mice.
source: In Ngl2-/- mice, horizontal cell axons frequently stray into the outer nuclear layer (Soto et al., 2013). Stray processes were less abundant in horizontal cells targeted by our AAV-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 strategy (Figure 2—figure supplement 3)
evidence: Quantitative data showing differences in mistargeting phenotypes between AAV-mediated knockout and germline knockout

claim: Mistargeting of horizontal cell axons may involve non-cell-autonomous actions of NGL2 or may be reduced by delays in AAV-mediated removal compared to germline knockouts.
source: indicating either that mistargeting involves non-cell-autonomous actions of NGL2, or that delays in the AAV-mediated removal of NGL2 reduced the severity of laminar targeting deficits compared to germline knockouts.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the observed differences in mistargeting phenotypes

claim: Removal of neuroligin-2 from the medial prefrontal cortex of adult mice reduces the number of inhibitory synapses.
source: In the medial prefrontal cortex of adult mice, removal of neuroligin-2 reduces the number of inhibitory synapses (Liang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: In the cerebellum, parallel fiber inputs are lost after deletion of GluRδ2 in mature Purkinje cells.
source: In the cerebellum, parallel fiber inputs are lost after deletion of GluRδ2 in mature Purkinje cells (Takeuchi et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: Synaptic CAMs stabilize synapses and the cues that maintain circuits overlap with those that govern their formation.
source: Together, these findings indicate that synaptic CAMs stabilize synapses and that the cues that maintain circuits overlap with those that govern their formation.
evidence: Inference drawn from multiple lines of evidence including this study and cited studies

claim: NGL2 appears to act cell-autonomously in the hippocampus, where knockdown in individual pyramidal cells lowers spine density.
source: NGL2 appears to act similarly in the hippocampus, where knockdown in individual pyramidal cells lowers spine density (DeNardo et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: NGL2 levels limit synapse formation in wild-type retinas.
source: The observation that AAV-mediated overexpression of NGL2 in horizontal cells in wild-type and Ngl2-/- mice elevates axon tip density above wild-type levels (Figure 5) suggests that NGL2 levels control connectivity bidirectionally and limit synapse formation in wild-type retinas.
evidence: Inference based on experimental data showing increased synapse density with NGL2 overexpression

claim: Spine density in the hippocampus is reduced in Cadm1-/- mice and increased in transgenic mice overexpressing SynCAM1.
source: Similarly, spine density in the hippocampus is reduced in Cadm1-/- mice and increased in transgenic mice overexpressing SynCAM1, the protein encoded by Cadm1 (Robbins et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: NGL2 interacts trans-synaptically with netrin-G2.
source: NGL2 interacts trans-synaptically with netrin-G2 (DeNardo et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2006; Nishimura-Akiyoshi et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple previous studies

claim: The auxiliary Ca2+ channel subunit α2δ2 mediates trans-synaptic interactions.
source: Similarly, the auxiliary Ca2+ channel subunit α2δ2, which mediates trans-synaptic interactions (Fell et al., 2016), restricts axon growth in developing and mature mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons (Tedeschi et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: The auxiliary Ca2+ channel subunit α2δ2 restricts axon growth in developing and mature mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons.
source: Similarly, the auxiliary Ca2+ channel subunit α2δ2, which mediates trans-synaptic interactions (Fell et al., 2016), restricts axon growth in developing and mature mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons (Tedeschi et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: Ig-domain-containing CAMs contribute to axon maintenance in C. elegans.
source: and Ig-domain-containing CAMs contribute to axon maintenance in C. elegans (Aurelio et al., 2002; Cherra and Jin, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: Synaptic CAMs can control the size of neurite arbors during development and at maturity.
source: Together, these results indicate that synaptic CAMs can control the size of neurite arbors during development and at maturity.
evidence: Inference drawn from multiple lines of evidence including this study and cited studies

claim: A homeostatic relationship between neurite growth and synapse formation was reported for aCC neurons in Drosophila embryos.
source: A homeostatic relationship between these processes was reported for aCC neurons in Drosophila embryos (Tripodi et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: Bidirectional manipulations in the number of input synapses on aCC dendrites elicit opposite changes in arbor size.
source: Bidirectional manipulations in the number of input synapses on aCC dendrites elicit opposite changes in arbor size (Tripodi et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: Neurite growth appears positively coupled to synapse formation of axons and dendrites in the optic tectum of Xenopus and Zebrafish, respectively.
source: By contrast, neurite growth appears positively coupled to synapse formation of axons and dendrites in the optic tectum of Xenopus and Zebrafish, respectively (Niell et al., 2004; Ruthazer et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: In the mouse retina, the size and morphology of bipolar cell axons and ganglion cell dendrites are established and maintained independent of connections between them.
source: In the mouse retina, the size and morphology of bipolar cell axons and ganglion cell dendrites are established and maintained independent of connections between them (Johnson and Kerschensteiner, 2014; Kerschensteiner et al., 2009; Morgan et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: Retinal degeneration is the most common heritable cause of visual impairment.
source: We speculate that AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 might help preserve outer retinal connectivity in retinal degeneration, the most common heritable cause of visual impairment (Sohocki et al., 2001; Jones et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 might help preserve outer retinal connectivity in retinal degeneration.
source: We speculate that AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 might help preserve outer retinal connectivity in retinal degeneration, the most common heritable cause of visual impairment (Sohocki et al., 2001; Jones et al., 2012).
evidence: Speculative statement about potential therapeutic application based on study findings

claim: Transplantation of stem-cell-derived photoreceptors is being explored as a treatment for late stages of retinal degeneration.
source: Transplantation of stem-cell-derived photoreceptors is being explored as a treatment for late stages of retinal degeneration (Gamm et al., 2015; Wahlin et al., 2017; Chirco et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 in second-order neurons could promote the integration of stem-cell-derived photoreceptors into host circuits.
source: Our results suggest that AAV-mediated expression of NGL2 in second-order neurons (i.e., bipolar and horizontal cells) could promote the integration of stem-cell-derived photoreceptors into host circuits and help restore vision.
evidence: Speculative statement about potential therapeutic application based on study findings

claim: Two sgRNAs (sgNGL21 and sgNGL22) reliably introduced frame-shifting insertions and deletions near the start of the open reading frame of Ngl2.
source: We identified two short guide RNAs (sgRNAs) that reliably introduced frame-shifting insertions and deletions (indels) near the start of the open reading frame of Ngl2 (see Materials and methods).
evidence: Experimental validation in Neuro-2a cells showing recombination rates of 60% and 68% for sgNGL21 and sgNGL22 respectively

claim: AAV1/2 chimeric virions readily infect horizontal cells.
source: Briefly, AAV1/2 chimeric virions, which readily infect horizontal cells (Soto et al., 2013), were produced by co-transfecting HEK293 cells
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study

claim: Both sgRNAs tested drastically increased horizontal cell axon size in Cas9 mice.
source: Both sgRNAs tested drastically increased horizontal cell axon size in Cas9 mice (Cas9 sgNGL21n = 35, 6 mice, p<10−7 for comparison to Cas9 YFP, Cas9 sgNGL22n = 32, 7 mice, p=10−9 for comparison to Cas9 YFP)
evidence: Statistical analysis of quantitative measurements showing significant increases in axon territory

claim: Both sgRNAs tested reduced horizontal cell axon tip densities in Cas9 mice.
source: and reduced tip densities (Cas9 sgNGL21n = 29, 5 mice, p < 10-12 for comparison to Cas9 YFP, Cas9 sgNGL22n = 16, 3 mice, p<0.001 for comparison to Cas9 YFP).
evidence: Statistical analysis of quantitative measurements showing significant reductions in tip density

claim: Horizontal cells infected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT (sgNGL22) in Cas9 mice had more severe mistargeting phenotypes than horizontal cells in wild-type mice infected with AAV-YFP or AAV-sgNGL2-tdT, or horizontal cells in Cas9 mice infected with AAV-YFP.
source: Horizontal cells infected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT (sgNGL22, not sgNGL21) in Cas9 mice had more severe mistargeting phenotypes than horizontal cells in wild-type mice infected with AAV-YFP (p<0.02) or AAV-sgNGL2-tdT (p<0.004), or horizontal cells in Cas9 mice infected with AAV-YFP (p<0.004).
evidence: Statistical analysis of categorical data on mistargeting phenotypes

claim: Horizontal cells in Cas9 mice infected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT had less severe mistargeting phenotypes than horizontal cells in Ngl2-/- mice infected with AAV-YFP.
source: Horizontal cells in Cas9 mice infected with AAV-sgNGL2-tdT (sgNGL22 and sgNGL21) in Cas9 mice had less severe mistargeting phenotypes than horizontal cells in Ngl2-/- mice infected with AAV-YFP (p<0.002).
evidence: Statistical analysis of categorical data on mistargeting phenotypes

claim: Horizontal cell axon tips penetrate rod spherules.
source: Horizontal cell dendrite clusters at cone terminals and horizontal cell axon tips, which penetrate rod spherules (Peichl and González-Soriano, 1994; Wässle, 2004), were identified by eye in confocal image stacks
evidence: Established anatomical knowledge supported by citations

claim: NGL2 promotes the formation, maintenance, and restoration of synapses in the developing and mature retina.
source: Thus, NGL2 promotes the formation, maintenance, and restoration of synapses in the developing and mature retina, and restricts axon growth throughout life.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on all experimental findings in the study

claim: NGL2 restricts axon growth throughout life.
source: Thus, NGL2 promotes the formation, maintenance, and restoration of synapses in the developing and mature retina, and restricts axon growth throughout life.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on all experimental findings in the study
